description: Add a `deviceSync` settings shape to rmm_integrations.settings: { enabled: boolean, intervalMinutes: number }, read with defaults rather than backfilled by migration
parseRmmDeviceSyncState(row) returns { active, syncEnabled, intervalMinutes } with intervalMinutes clamped to 15..1440 and defaulting to 60
deviceSync.enabled defaults to false for existing integrations so no tenant gains recurring API load without opting in
Define RMM_DEVICE_SYNC_PROVIDERS as a list independent of RMM_ALERT_POLLING_PROVIDERS
Add RMM_DEVICE_SYNC_JOB = 'rmm-device-sync' job name constant alongside the existing RMM job constants
Register an rmm-device-sync job handler with the IJobRunner registry so both pg-boss (CE) and Temporal (EE) can execute it
rmm-device-sync job data carries { tenantId, integrationId, provider }
Recurring device-sync jobs use singletonKey `rmm-device-sync:<tenant>:<integration>` so one integration cannot accumulate duplicate schedules
Device-sync schedules are created from intervalMinutesToCron(intervalMinutes), reusing the existing helper
The RMM polling reconciler also reconciles device-sync schedules, creating jobs for newly eligible integrations
The reconciler cancels a device-sync schedule when the integration is deactivated
The reconciler cancels a device-sync schedule when deviceSync.enabled becomes false
The reconciler recreates a device-sync schedule at the new cadence when intervalMinutes changes
The reconciler leaves an unchanged, healthy device-sync schedule untouched (no churn on every pass)
The reconciler skips providers absent from RMM_DEVICE_SYNC_PROVIDERS without logging an error per pass
The device-sync handler resolves the provider's sync strategy and no-ops with a warning when none is registered for that provider
A successful scheduled run sets rmm_integrations.last_incremental_sync_at
A successful scheduled run sets last_sync_at and sync_status = 'completed' and clears sync_error
A failed scheduled run records sync_error and sync_status = 'failed' without cancelling the schedule
A scheduled run for a suspended tenant exits without calling the provider API
Concurrent runs for the same integration are prevented (singleton semantics honoured on both backends)
Define a shared syncDevicesIncremental strategy interface that every provider strategy can implement
The delta cursor resolves as last_incremental_sync_at ?? last_full_sync_at ?? now-24h, matching NinjaOne's existing semantics
NinjaOne: the scheduled job calls the existing syncDevicesIncremental strategy rather than a new code path
NinjaOne: verify and document the `since` parameter's server-side semantics against the NinjaOne API before relying on it
NinjaOne: the manual server action and the scheduled job share one implementation with no behavioural divergence
Level.io: determine whether the device list endpoint supports any server-side filter that avoids a full page walk; record the finding
Level.io: implement syncDevicesIncremental filtering devices by last_seen_at against the delta cursor
Level.io: incremental sync walks cursor pagination (starting_after, limit 100) to completion
Level.io: incremental sync writes only devices whose snapshot changed, leaving untouched rows' updated_at stable
Tanium: implement syncDevicesIncremental, or document that only a full sync is possible and schedule it at a low cadence
TacticalRMM: investigate why no integration has ever completed a sync and record the root cause
TacticalRMM: implement or repair device sync so a manual sync succeeds before any schedule is enabled
TacticalRMM: implement syncDevicesIncremental once the base sync works
Huntress: determine whether a device sync path exists at all; if not, exclude it from RMM_DEVICE_SYNC_PROVIDERS and record why
Huntress: device sync must not disturb the incident poller's use of last_incremental_sync_at as its cursor
Add a Device sync enable/disable toggle to each connected integration's panel in Integrations → RMM
Add an interval control (minutes) to the integration panel, constrained to the same 15..1440 bounds enforced server-side
The panel shows last synced, derived from last_incremental_sync_at ?? last_full_sync_at
The panel surfaces sync_error when the last scheduled run failed
Saving the interval persists to settings.deviceSync and takes effect within one reconciler pass without a restart
The Device sync control is hidden or disabled for providers not in RMM_DEVICE_SYNC_PROVIDERS
The manual Full sync button retains its existing behaviour unchanged
All new UI strings are wired through useTranslation and added to the English pack (no hardcoded copy)
New interactive elements carry kebab-case ids for the UI reflection system
A server action persists deviceSync settings with permission checks via withAuth
Level.io deviceMapper populates agent_version from the device payload — NOT POSSIBLE: the Level.io API does not expose this (see SCRATCHPAD)
Level.io deviceMapper populates wan_ip, replacing the hardcoded null — NOT POSSIBLE: the Level.io API does not expose this (see SCRATCHPAD)
Level.io deviceMapper populates pending_patches
Level.io deviceMapper populates pending_software_patches — NOT POSSIBLE: the Level.io API does not expose this (see SCRATCHPAD)
Level.io deviceMapper populates failed_patches — NOT POSSIBLE: the Level.io API does not expose this (see SCRATCHPAD)
Any of the five fields the Level.io API genuinely does not expose is documented in SCRATCHPAD.md rather than left silently null
Device sync schedules work on CE via pg-boss cron for providers available in CE
Device sync schedules work on EE via Temporal Schedules
CE degrades cleanly for providers whose sync engine lives under ee/ (no import failure, no crashloop)
The reconciler tolerates an integration row deleted between scan and schedule creation
All device-sync queries include tenant in WHERE and JOIN clauses per the CitusDB rules
Enabling device sync for one integration does not create schedules for that tenant's other integrations
